intentAndPurpose.intent: Numeric input control with increment and decrement buttons for bounded integer values.

rules.name: high
useWhen: primary quantity input requiring high emphasis

props.name: appearance
props.description: Multi-accent appearance role. Controls all tokens. `'auto'` or omit: inherit nearest `<Surface>` effective role (see `useSurfaceAppearance`), else `'secondary'` when outside any Surface (same pattern as Badge, different root fallback).

props.name: attention
props.description: Attention level controls visual weight. Default: 'medium'

props.name: className
props.description: Additional class name

props.name: condensed
props.description: Whether to use condensed height. Default: false. Button type only (ignored for `type="input"`).

props.name: data-testid
props.description: Test ID

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Default value (uncontrolled)

props.name: direction
props.description: Visual direction. Default: 'ltr' keeps decrement left and increment right; 'rtl' mirrors the visual order.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Whether the stepper is disabled

props.name: end
props.description: Optional increment control (right in LTR, left in RTL). Same rules as {@link StepperProps.start}. Omitted: default add icon. `partProps.incrementButton.render` overrides. **Semantics:** this slot always drives **increase** behaviour.

props.name: error
props.description: Whether the stepper is in error state

props.name: fullWidth
props.description: Stretch to the parent width; value field expands between − / +. Default: false.

props.name: max
props.description: Maximum allowed value

props.name: min
props.description: Minimum allowed value

props.name: onChange
props.type: (event: SyntheticEvent | null, value: number | null) => void
props.description: Change handler — Base UI standard signature

props.name: partProps
props.type: { root?: ComponentPropsWithRef<'div'>; input?: ComponentPropsWithRef<'input'>; incrementButton?: ComponentPropsWithRef<'button'>; decrementButton?: ComponentPropsWithRef<'button'>; }
props.description: Props for internal Base UI parts. Use for primitive-level overrides, not public content slots.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Whether the stepper is read-only

props.name: required
props.description: Whether the field is required

props.name: shiftMultiplier
props.description: Jump by larger amount when holding Shift. Maps to Base UI's largeStep.

props.name: size
props.description: Size preset. Default: 'm'

props.name: start
props.description: Optional decrement control (left in LTR, right in RTL). Must be a **single `<IconButton />` element** whose root accepts merged props and ref from the NumberField. Uses Base UI `render` on `Decrement`. Omitted: default remove icon. `partProps.decrementButton.render` overrides. **Semantics:** this slot always drives **decrease** behaviour (not “leading” in the abstract).

props.name: step
props.description: Step increment. Default: 1

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles

props.name: subtleMotion
props.description: Disable value scroll and pill width animations — value and size update instantly. Default: false

props.name: type
props.description: Chrome type. Default: `'button'` (pill). `'input'` is the Input-like rounded rect. Figma dependencies: `size="xs"` only applies to input. Input `low` matches `medium` (auto(neutral) stroke); high fill is auto(neutral) Minimal.

props.description: Controlled value

codeSnippets.title: Basic Usage
codeSnippets.code:
import { Stepper } from '@oneui/ui';

<Stepper defaultValue={1} min={0} max={10} />

codeSnippets.title: Controlled
codeSnippets.code: <Stepper value={qty} onChange={(_, v) => setQty(v ?? 0)} min={1} max={99} />

interactionBehavior.summary: Stepper is a Base UI NumberField whose visible value is an odometer, not the native input: each place's digit strip translateY-rolls on a CSS `transform` transition (`--Motion-Duration-L` / `--Motion-Easing-Transition-Moderate`) so a held auto-repeat retargets instead of restarting. When the digit count changes the pill width animates too — each `.place` transitions `width`, a new place entering from `@starting-style { width: 0 }` and a removed one collapsing to `0` on `[data-exiting]`, so 9→10 eases the capsule wider and 10→9 shrinks it. The affected leading digit is a `.riser` that translateY-rolls in from below (or sinks out) in sync, its entrance staggered by `--Stepper-leadDelay` (`--Motion-Offset-L`); `prefers-reduced-motion` and `data-subtle-motion` set `transition: none` on all of it. The +/− controls are IconButtons. A comment on `.button` zeros `--Motion-Tap-Scale-Default`, but those 1:1 buttons actually scale UP via `--Motion-Tap-Scale-Up`; `overflow: clip` on the pill is what keeps the overlay inside. Direct typing reveals the real input; a +/− press that focuses the input on purpose does not.
hover: Hover lives on the inner IconButtons, not the pill. Stepper remaps their ghost hover slots onto its attention tokens: `--{Role}-Bold-Hover` at `attention="high"`, `--{Role}-Subtle-Hover` at medium, `--Neutral-Hover` (auto) at low and for every `type="input"` attention.
Those IconButton hover fills are `(hover: hover)`-guarded in IconButton's own CSS, so a touch tap never leaves a stuck overlay.
The pill background itself does not change on hover.
press: Press fill on +/− follows the same remapped slots: `--{Role}-Bold-Pressed` / `--{Role}-Subtle-Pressed` / `--Neutral-Pressed` by attention.

`.button` sets `--Motion-Tap-Scale-Default: 0` with a comment claiming this zeros IconButton squash. Current 1:1 IconButtons (Stepper uses sizes 4 / 6 / 8 / 10) actually scale UP via `--Motion-Tap-Scale-Up` (default 7%) — they do not read `--Motion-Tap-Scale-Default`. The pill's `overflow: clip` is what contains that grow so the overlay never paints outside the capsule.

Holding +/− uses Base UI `usePressAndHold`: the first tick steps, then auto-repeat continues to fire `incrementValue`. Releasing commits via `onValueCommitted`. The odometer transition retargets, so a hold scrolls continuously instead of restarting each tick.
At `min` / `max` that button is natively disabled by Base UI (`isAtBoundary`) and stops ticking.
focus: Keyboard focus on either +/− button draws the two-layer halo on the GROUP, not the button: `--Stroke-XL` gap in `--Surface-Halo-Gap` plus an outer `--Informative-Bold` ring (always Informative). Each IconButton's own `:focus-visible` ring is suppressed (`box-shadow: none`).
The halo selector is `:has(button:focus-visible)` only — focusing the value input to type does not paint it.
`[data-force-state="focus"]` on the group mirrors the same halo for documentation.
keyboard: The native input is always mounted (visually hidden until edit). `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` step by `step` (default 1). `Shift+Arrow` uses `largeStep` (`step * shiftMultiplier`, default 10). `Alt+Arrow` uses Base UI's `smallStep`.
`Home` / `End` jump to `min` / `max` only when those bounds are passed; without them the keys are left to the browser.

Typing digits enters edit mode (`data-editing`): the odometer hides, the input shows its caret, and NumberField commits on `Enter` or blur — not on each keystroke. Arrow-key stepping goes through `setValue`, not a DOM `input` event, so it does not trip edit mode.
A +/− `pointerdown` sets `steppingRef` so the focus Base UI then moves onto the input (non-touch only) does not swap to edit mode and kill the roll animation.
disabled: `disabled` adds `.disabled` on the group: `--Disabled-Opacity` and `pointer-events: none`. The ROOT (`:has(.disabled)`) sets `cursor: not-allowed`, so the not-allowed cursor is observable — the opposite of the Button gap, because the cursor lives on the still-hit-testable wrapper.
`readOnly` is different: the group gets `pointer-events: none` and `cursor: default`, the +/− buttons are `visibility: hidden`, and the input is `readOnly`. It does not dim.

At min/max only the exhausted IconButton is natively disabled; because that button also has IconButton's `pointer-events: none`, its own `not-allowed` cursor is not observable (the known gap), while the rest of the stepper still works.
touch: IconButton hover overlays never apply on touch-only devices; the remapped pressed fill plus IconButton's 7% scale-up (clipped by the pill) are the tap response.
Base UI's stepper-button focus-the-input behaviour is documented as non-touch only, so a finger tap on +/− does not steal focus into the hidden field.
